a_records.quote: Theorem (1) Let X ∼ MWR(σ1 , λ1 ) and Y ∼ MWR(σ2 , λ2 ), Then the following results hold true i) If σ1 = σ2 and λ1 > λ2 then X ≤lr Y , X ≤hr Y and X ≤st Y
a_records.family: Modified weighted Rayleigh MWR(σ,λ): fW(x) = ((λ²+1)/σ²) x e^{−(λ²+1)x²/(2σ²)}-type density (weighted Rayleigh; λ = 0 reduces to Rayleigh)
a_records.compared: two MWR distributions differing only in λ

hypotheses.formal: equal scale σ, larger weight parameter λ

conclusion.direction: X <=lr Y, X <=hr Y and X <=st Y (likelihood ratio, hazard rate, usual stochastic — chain via lr ⇒ hr ⇒ st)

a_records.ambiguity: Definitions printed: X <=st Y iff FX >= FY; X <=hr Y iff hX >= hY; X <=lr Y iff fX/fY decreasing. Proof shows d/dx log(fX/fY) < 0 for λ1 > λ2.
